title: Abba Poemen
hookLine: teach your mouth to say what is in your heart
tomorrow: why does a well-known life story open by talking to God?

cards: How are you? Fine. Sounds great.

No worries, all good. Whole days can run on sentences like these, while something else is going on underneath. Desert monks left town for the quiet, so you might expect their advice on speech to be two words: talk less.
Is keeping quiet the same as being honest? An elder named Abba Poemen says no, and asks for something harder.

teach.b: His saying is one line: teach your mouth to say what is in your heart. Notice the verb. Teach.

The mouth has to learn this. Left alone, it says what's easy, or polite, or safe, or what makes us look good, while the heart says something else. Poemen wants the two to line up, and that cuts both ways.

teach.h: NO WARM WORDS OVER A COLD HEART.
teach.b: No flattery, no pretending to agree, no warm words over a cold heart. And the heart has to be worth saying out loud, which turns the work back inside.

teach.h: OUT OF THE ABUNDANCE OF THE HEART.
teach.b: Jesus says something close in Matthew's Gospel: "for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh." Sooner or later, what fills the heart comes out. Poemen asks for it on purpose.
Another saying under his name gives the answer to today's question, and it's the one to tell a friend. Someone can sit in silence all day and still be chattering inside, if they're condemning others.
And someone can talk from morning to night and still keep silence, if nothing they say is empty.
So silence isn't a word count.
It's whether the words match what's true. For this week, that means the next fine you don't mean, and one honest sentence, said kindly, in its place.

how: Christians read the sayings of Abba Poemen for guidance on honest speech and on silence, in monastic communities and outside them.

games.q: a friend plays you the song she wrote and asks what you think. you love the verse; the chorus doesn't work yet. what fits Poemen?
o: 'it's perfect!', since being kind matters more than being true.
say nothing much, since silence can't hurt anyone.
say what you love, and kindly, that the chorus isn't there yet.
games.why: teach your mouth to say what is in your heart: no warm words over a cold heart, and no cold words either. the true thing, kindly.

practice: Bring to mind one quick yes, or one fine, that didn't match your heart this week. Find the plain, kind sentence you actually meant, and say it out loud once, quietly, to the room. Then sit with how it sounds.

wordCard.voice: Abba Poemen. A desert elder who taught the mouth to say what the heart holds, and saw that silence is about truth, not word count.

carryVoice: Your line: heart and mouth together. The mouth learns it slowly, one honest sentence at a time. Bye for now.
